caseStudy.title: YAMVIP
caseStudy.lead: YAMVIP (Yet Another MVI Presenter): a multiplatform MVI engine that shares presentation logic between Android and iOS, with a strict split between Model, UIState, Intent and Effect.

brief.title: The idea
text: Sharing business logic in Kotlin is common; sharing presentation logic is harder. YAMVIP gives both apps the same presenters, so screens behave the same on Android and iOS and can be unit-tested once.
It favours convention over configuration and a good developer experience.

contributions.title: What I did
items: Worked on the presenter pattern: every presenter extends YamviPresenter, typed by its Model, UIState and Effect.
Separated the internal Model from the UIState that the UI renders, joined by a mapper.
Handled intents with a reducer that produces the next Model, exposed as StateFlow.
Kept Effects for one-shot events only, as a last resort.
Wrote examples and discussed the patterns with the team.

outcome.text: A shared presentation layer the team used as a reference, later part of the KMP Template.
